Status values: `accepted` · `superseded by ADR-00xx` · `deprecated`

## Adding one

1. Take the next number, copy [`_template.md`](_template.md) to
   `NNNN-<english-slug>.md`.
2. Fill it in. Keep it to roughly 15-40 lines.
3. Run `bash .claude/scripts/docs-regen.sh` — the index above regenerates itself.

## Three rules

- **One decision, one file.** A second file discussing the same thing means the first
  decision was never settled.
- **Append-only.** An `accepted` ADR is **not edited**. Changing your mind means a new
  ADR that records `supersedes ADR-0007`, and flipping the old one to `superseded by`.
- **Write it when it is settled**, not at the end of the session. A long session's
  context can be compacted before it ends, and the reasoning is the first thing lost.

## When an ADR is needed

Needed: choosing a library / framework / datastore · moving a module boundary · picking
between two or more reasonable ways to solve something · accepting a long-lived
limitation.

Not needed: fixing a bug · adding a feature that follows an existing pattern · a
decision that could be reversed in ten minutes.

## Where these came from

ADR-0001 through ADR-0016 were written on 2026-09-13, back-dated to when each decision
was actually made. They were extracted from `docs/session-log.md` and the two design
specs under `docs/superpowers/specs/`, all of which were deleted in the same pass and
remain in git history.
